_why: A waiver is a RECEIPT FOR A KNOWN DEFECT WITH A DEADLINE ON IT, never a place to hide one.
scripts/check_published_versions.py fails on any version a document advertises that the
registry does not serve. An entry here downgrades one (file, coordinate) pair to a loud
::warning:: until 'expires', and ONLY because the file belongs to a lane that is already
fixing it — this repository is edited by several agents at once and a cross-lane edit
collides. Two rules keep the list honest, both enforced by the checker:
* AN EXPIRED WAIVER IS A HARD FAILURE. The date is not advisory.
* A WAIVER WHOSE CLAIM HAS BECOME CORRECT IS A HARD FAILURE. Delete it. The list can
only shrink — the same rule swift-examples.yml puts on its KNOWN_BROKEN list.
★THE LIST IS EMPTY, AND IT GOT THERE THE WAY IT IS SUPPOSED TO. It was opened on
2026-09-22 with two entries: android/README.md advertised essence2-android 0.2.0 and
expression2-android 0.3.0 while Maven Central served 0.5.12 and 0.4.8. The android lane
landed c30e81c the same day with both corrected, the checker raised STALE WAIVER on both
entries, and they were deleted. Under a day, open to closed, with the gate doing the
noticing. Reopen it the same way: an owner, a reason, a date.
If you are about to add an entry: the fix is almost always one line in the file itself.
Prefer '<!-- version-check-ignore: reason -->' on the line, in your own file, for the one
case a waiver is not for — a DATED MEASUREMENT, where the old version number is the point.
